mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such co-occurrence events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% while the unemployment rate is below 4.0% indicates supply-side disruptions in an otherwise tight labor market, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such co-occurrence events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, regardless of prior level, signals an aggressive tightening stance that immediately raises risk-free rates and equity valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Change in FEDFUNDS > 0.75% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 1% coincident with an unemployment rate below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and pressures profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a high-growth regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered late-cycle events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly real retail sales (RSAFS) increase of more than 1% while the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises less than 0.2% in the same month signals improving demand without inflationary pressure, supporting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month + 1% AND CPIAUCSL < previous month + 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes during inflation-cooling periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals a secular demand shortfall, which erodes earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.
